query: The Spoon Will Fall At breakfast Seraphine says, without looking up, "Practise on small things. Spoons. Doors. The weather. Never people, not yet." Then she looks at you, quite clearly, for once. Foretell small things all day The spoon falls. The door sticks. It rains at four. By evening it unnerves you how well it works, and you catch yourself foretelling the soup. Ask what "not yet" means "Later," she says, then, "I mean that exactly." She doesn't explain. She does pass you the salt before you've asked for it.
